items.title: Wire dist generate --check into a real CI gate for the create-release pairing
body: Batch 24 T3b fix round 1 (task-3b-review.json, important issue 2): crates/houserules/tests/dist_workspace_config.rs pins dist-workspace.toml's create-release = false and release.yml's upload-not-create shape by two independent substrings, with no gate that re-derives one from the other. The file's own doc comment used to claim `dist generate --check` runs in CI and catches drift; it does not. No job in .github/workflows/ci.yml and no task in mise.toml installs or runs `dist` at all, and re-derived live: a scratch clone of the tree at batch 24 T3b fix round 1 with a one-line hand-edit appended to release.yml exits 0 from `dist generate --check` under this repository's own allow-dirty = ["ci"], and exits 255 with an 'out of date contents' diff only once allow-dirty is cleared to []. The comment is corrected to state this plainly; this item tracks making it a real gate instead.

Feasibility, re-derived live at the same fix round: mise's own registry carries cargo-dist (`mise registry | grep dist` -> `aqua:axodotdev/cargo-dist github:axodotdev/cargo-dist cargo:cargo-dist`); `mise install` against a one-line scratch mise.toml (`[tools]\n"cargo-dist" = "0.32.0"`) installed a working `dist` binary via the aqua backend in one step on this Linux development environment, GitHub artifact attestation verified. Linux install is proven; macOS and Windows are not (no such host here), and ci.yml's `rust` job runs a 3-OS matrix (ubuntu/macos/windows) that would also pick up any tool this repository's global mise.toml [tools] table names -- adding cargo-dist there unscoped risks an untested install path on two OSes no existing tool in that table exercises.

Proposed fix: add cargo-dist to mise.toml's [tools], pinned to the same version as dist-workspace.toml's cargo-dist-version (security-hygiene.exact-pins), scoped to the one OS the check actually needs -- mise's own docs name an `os` tool-option for exactly this (mise.jdx.dev/configuration.html, checked 2026-09-13); verify its literal TOML syntax against current docs before use, since the fetched page named the option without a worked example. Add `dist generate --check` as a step in mise.toml's `lint` task (which runs only in ci.yml's ubuntu-only `checks` job, so the rust job's macOS/Windows legs need no new tool at all). Re-run the two exit-code probes above against the real gate (0 clean, 255 on a hand-edit) before shipping, and update dist_workspace_config.rs's doc comment once the gate is real.

Deferred out of batch 24 T3b's fix round per that review's own escape hatch (a full regen gate is shipped only when proven safe wherever it runs; otherwise the honest-comment version plus this deferral note): the CI-wide, 3-OS blast radius of a mise.toml [tools] change is not something to land untested in a fix round with no CI run available here to verify it against first.

items.title: release-please misses commits that change the embedded template/ payload but not crates/houserules/**
body: HR-073's release-type: rust at crates/houserules moved release-please's commit attribution off the repository root: CommitSplit.split (commit-split.ts:99) now counts a commit toward the crate's next version only when it touches crates/houserules/**, since the ROOT_PROJECT_PATH special case that used to assign every commit (manifest.ts:700-701) no longer applies. crates/houserules/src/install.rs:232-234 embeds `../../template/` into the shipped binary via #[derive(RustEmbed)], so a commit that changes only template/ (or README.md, or another root-level path) changes shipped code and, under the new attribution, opens no release PR at all.

Measured over v0.2.0-alpha..6aa19e0 (batch 20 T5 fix round 1 review): 82 of 119 commits touch no path under crates/houserules/, and 7 of 27 feat/fix commits are unattributed under the new package path -- four of them (7460c77b feat(template), 6ac1aaa7 fix(template), 719d3f58 fix(tools), 101555ef fix(template)) change the embedded payload directly, per t5-evidence/hr081-template-payload-commits.sh's own enumeration by touched path rather than commit subject (fix round 2: a subject-scoped read of the same range missed 719d3f58, 'fix(tools): validate rejects incomplete terminal reports', which touches no crates/houserules/ path and two template/ files). Today enough crate-side commits ride along that a release PR still opens; a cycle whose only changes are template/, README.md, or the knowledge base would silently ship nothing.

The package path is not the thing to change: release-type rust at '.' (the root) would take the Rust strategy's workspace branch and push a CargoToml update for the root manifest, which cargo-toml.ts:37-40 throws on ('is not a package manifest') since the root Cargo.toml carries no [package] section under this workspace's virtual-manifest shape -- reviewer-confirmed and re-verified by the implementer. The gap needs a different remedy, not a reversal of HR-073's ruling.

Candidate remedies (this item carries the question, not the answer): (a) an extra-files or component-mapping addition to release-please-config.json that attributes template/** changes to the crate's own path for commit-attribution purposes; (b) a documented pre-release rule that a payload-changing commit always rides alongside a crate-side commit before a release is cut, checked by hand or by a gate. Owner picks.

MECHANISM (task-1 fix round 4, provisional pending owner ratification at the batch report): remedy (b), concretized. crates/houserules/payload.stamp records a sha256 digest of template/'s tracked file set, recomputed and compared by payload-stamp-gate (crates/houserules/src/bin/payload-stamp-gate.rs), wired into mise run lint (houserules.payload-stamp-gate). That gate is a TREE-LEVEL check only: a branch splitting the template/ edit from the stamp regeneration across two commits still passes it at the tip. Fix round 5 closed that gap: houserules check-commit now also runs this entry's own co-change check (if template/**, then crates/houserules/payload.stamp) per commit, over the PR's full range in CI, so a split commit pair fails before merge, not only a stale tree.

Still gating this item's own close: the mechanism above is proven by source-level review and a full-pipeline simulation against real git history (batch-24 task-1's own t1-evidence/), never by a genuine release-please run. The first real template-only change that lands on main after T2 -- one commit touching template/ and crates/houserules/payload.stamp together, nothing else -- is that live proof.
Source: batch 20 T5 fix round 1 review (task-5-review.json), important finding 1.

CLOSED by live proof, 2026-09-15: batch 26's merge put ea17fc6 feat(template) on main - a commit whose only crates/houserules/** path is payload.stamp. release-please run 34951127224 opened release PR #28 (chore(main): release 1.1.0) whose changelog carries exactly that commit as its one feature: the stamp pairing attributed the template-payload change to the crate and drove the minor bump. The release PR itself is owner-attended.

items.title: houserules update self-updates the installed binary
body: Owner (2026-09-15): 'houserules update does update a repo but it doesn't update the installed houserules binary. It should.' Design at spec time: the mechanism must respect the install channel (shell installer, mise, direct download) - a mise-managed binary is mise's to update, a self-replaced one needs the dist install receipt. Cluster with HR-134 and HR-135.

items.title: Update-available notice on every command when a newer release exists
body: Owner (2026-09-15): when a new houserules version is published, the binary states that an update is available on every command, as a small header, like other CLI tools do. Design at spec time: version check against the GitHub latest release with a local cache and a short TTL; never a network call per invocation; silent on network failure; an opt-out env var. Cluster with HR-133 and HR-135.

items.title: Install path: does ~/.cargo/bin make sense for a toolchain-neutral binary?
body: Owner (2026-09-15): houserules currently installs into .cargo; 'I am asking myself if that makes sense for a pure binary that has nothing to do with rust anymore on the user systems.' The shell installer's target comes from dist-workspace.toml (cargo-dist install-path; CARGO_HOME is the default). Candidate: ~/.local/bin (XDG) with a PATH fallback. Needs an owner ruling; a move also needs a migration story for existing installs and feeds HR-133's self-update mechanism. Cluster with HR-133 and HR-134.

RULED (owner, 2026-09-15, design.md 5.86): ~/.local/bin is correct. The move needs the dist-workspace.toml install-path change plus a migration story for existing ~/.cargo/bin installs; it feeds HR-133's self-update mechanism. Scheduled batch 27.

items.title: Agent-agnostic kit: the seeded structures work with Codex and other non-Claude harnesses

items.title: Confirm aws-lc-sys builds clean on every rust-job OS and every release leg
body: HR-133's axoupdater dependency pulled in aws-lc-sys (rustls' crypto provider) transitively. Walked on paper at batch 27 T2 fix round 1: prebuilt-nasm is already active for aws-lc-sys in this tree (rustls and rustls-webpki's own "aws-lc-rs" features each request "aws-lc-rs/prebuilt-nasm", confirmed by `cargo tree -e features -p aws-lc-sys` and a verbose `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` build passing `--cfg feature="prebuilt-nasm"` to rustc), so no leg needs a real NASM install. Every platform's own native C toolchain should cover the rest: macOS (Xcode CLT), Windows (MSVC, both ci.yml's windows-latest `rust`-job leg and release.yml's windows-msvc leg, both on GitHub-hosted images that ship it), and the two musl release legs (`dist plan --output-format=json`'s own artifacts_matrix runs them un-containerized on ubuntu-22.04(-arm) with `packages_install: apt-get install musl-tools`, already dist's own provisioning, not ci.yml's).

None of this is proven by an actual build: only the ubuntu `checks` job's windows-gnu cross-check has really compiled aws-lc-sys in this task, and even that ran with a substitute llvm-mingw toolchain (no root available to install the real gcc-mingw-w64-x86-64 package in the sandbox). The `rust` job's macos-latest and windows-latest legs, and release.yml's five target legs, have not run since this dependency landed. Confirm all of them green at the first real PR and the first real release cut after this change; if any leg fails, the fix is almost certainly a dist-workspace.toml packages/build-environment addition (never a hand edit of the generated release.yml) or the missing system package on ci.yml's own runner.

Proven live 2026-09-15, both halves. PR #30 (batch 27): the `rust` job passed on ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, and windows-latest. The v1.1.0 release run: all five `build-local-artifacts` legs passed (x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, aarch64-unknown-linux-musl), then `build-global-artifacts`, `host`, and `announce`.

items.title: The tdd mode label is proven with the capture and commit timestamps
body: GitHub issue #36 (owner, 2026-09-30). The issue reports from the adopter project orrery, batch 1: process.tdd failed in 3 of 13 tasks, all three label failures - a RED capture taken after the commit was filed as `natural`. The task-reviewer template checks the label by hand, so each failure cost a review round.

Request. Before the implementer writes a `tdd` entry, the template has it run `stat -c %y <red capture>` and `git log -1 --format=%cI <commit>`, label the entry `natural` only when the capture predates the commit and `reconstructed` otherwise, and paste both timestamps in the entry. Optional deterministic arm: check-report-claims compares the capture's mtime with the commit time for every entry labeled `natural`.

Triage 2026-10-01: the template half changes .claude/agents/implementer.md, so process.evals-rerun applies. The deterministic arm needs a design answer first: a file mtime does not survive a copy or a checkout, so the check holds only inside the session that made the capture.

Delivered in batch 28. `check-report-claims` fails a `natural` entry whose RED capture file is newer than the newest commit the report lists; the finding reads `was modified <N> s after the newest listed commit <sha> (committed <T>)`. A tracked capture file is skipped. The corpus run over the 165 retained task reports compared 72 natural captures and flagged only a deliberate probe. The template's `tdd` bullet names the capture form. The deterministic arm holds only in the workspace that made the capture; the module doc's Limits list says so.

items.title: A script that builds a report validates its own output
body: GitHub issue #37 (owner, 2026-09-30). The issue reports from the adopter project orrery, batch 1: one task report failed `houserules validate` in a fix round (process.deliverables-json). The implementer built the report with a script; the template tells the implementer to validate a temporary copy before the move into place, and the builder script skipped that step.
Request. One line in .claude/agents/implementer.md: a script that builds a report runs `houserules validate` on its output and exits non-zero on failure.
Triage 2026-10-01: a template-only change; process.evals-rerun applies.

Delivered in batch 28, as two sentences in the edit rule of the implementer template: a script that builds or edits the report runs `houserules validate` on its output and exits non-zero when validation fails; while `self_audit` is still `null`, the only error it lets pass is `needs a non-null self_audit`. The second sentence refines the wording the owner approved.

items.title: stats aborts on a non-JSON deliverable; a draft report's first audit fails; the gates need git
body: GitHub issue #39 (owner, 2026-09-30): three tooling defects and one note, all seen in one batch of the adopter project orrery.

(1) `houserules stats <workspace>` exits 2 for the whole workspace on one unreadable file. Request: report unreadable files in a `skipped` field and continue; the task-reviewer template says that probe outputs go to `.txt` files. Triage 2026-10-01, reproduced: a non-JSON file named `task-*-audit*.json`, `task-*-review*.json`, or `task-*-report.json` makes stats exit 2 with `invalid JSON`; a non-JSON `.json` file with another name is ignored. The abort is tested behavior (crates/houserules/src/rules/stats.rs), and quality.gates-derive-their-scope requires a gate to fail loudly on unreadable input, so the request needs a ruling.

(2) The first audit of a draft report fails process.deliverables-json. The retrieval protocol has the implementer write the report with `self_audit: null` and then audit it with `--report`; the issue reports that this first audit fails the report-field check (`report lacks a value for self_audit`) and that stats later counts the draft as a violation. Request: skip the `self_audit` presence check when `--report` is given and the field is null, or let stats ignore `*-draft.json`. Triage 2026-10-01: not reproduced yet; the template line (`self_audit` is `null` until the next step) is confirmed.

(3) check-knowledge and check-backlog need a git top level. Request: a `--dir` fallback that resolves the root without git, or a sentence in the reviewer templates. Triage 2026-10-01, reproduced: in a `git archive | tar` copy both gates exit 2 with git's own `fatal: not a git repository`; both pass there with `--dir .`. The flag exists; the gap is the unnamed error and the missing template sentence.

(4) Note: .claude/evals/record.json is seeded as `[]`, and the branch-reviewer template asks for a comparison against it that cannot run until a baseline exists. Request: a seeded baseline or a documented first-run step.

Delivered in batch 28. (1) The `stats` abort stays and its error names the remedy; the task-reviewer template sends probe output to `.txt` files. (2) A single-report audit passes a draft's null `self_audit` with the row text `report field self_audit is present`; a `--workspace` audit stays strict, and `validate` keeps rejecting a null `self_audit` at `DONE` and `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS`. (3) A command outside a git repository prints `<cwd> is not inside a git repository; pass --dir <repository root>`. (4) The empty eval record is a defined state in the branch-reviewer template and the orchestrating skill.

items.title: Kit-owned files cite a seeded knowledge entry an adopter can delete; no gate flags the dangling id
body: GitHub issue #40 (owner, 2026-10-01). The issue reports that kit 1.1.0 does not ship process.evals-rerun although .claude/skills/orchestrating/SKILL.md (section Template evaluation) and .claude/agents/branch-reviewer.md cite it: in the adopter project orrery `houserules get process.evals-rerun` answered `unknown id`, two agent-template changes shipped with .claude/evals/record.json still `[]`, and no audit failed. Request: ship the entry as a standing rule with a deterministic co-change check, or remove the two sentences and the evals directory from the install.

Triage 2026-10-01: the premise does not hold. template/knowledge/process.json carries process.evals-rerun with its co-change check, and a fresh `init` from the 1.1.0 tree seeds it (`get` prints it). The adopter project deleted the entry in its own knowledge ruling after the install, with other seeded process entries, and restored it later.

The defect that remains, reproduced in a scratch install: with the entry deleted, `houserules check-knowledge` still passes while the kit-owned orchestrating skill and branch-reviewer template keep citing the id. Seeded knowledge is the adopter's to edit; kit-owned files are not. Candidate fixes for the spec: a check-knowledge lint that fails when a kit-owned file cites a knowledge id that does not resolve; a sentence in the migrating-knowledge skill that names the seeded entries the kit-owned files depend on.

Delivered in batch 28. `check-knowledge` fails when a kit-owned file cites, as a backticked id of a seeded topic, an entry the knowledge base does not hold. The finding names two ways out for a seeded id (restore the entry, or list the citing file in `overrides`) and the way out for an id the kit never seeded. The kit-side test found one such id in the shipped finishing-a-feature skill, `knowledge-base.cite-durable-refs`; the citation was removed. Every install of 0.3.0 to 1.1.0 fails the new lint until `houserules update` runs (HR-154). Side effects of the remedy are in HR-151.

items.title: A balancing mechanism against micro-management and over-bureaucratizing in review rounds
body: Owner (2026-09-15): 'i observe that fix and review rounds have become longer due to menial defects that are more adhering to a protocol than actually producing valuable output. We need to introduce a balancing mechanism against micro-management and over-bureaucratizing.' Observed in batch 27: T2 took five review rounds and T4 three; several late rounds turned on prose wording, comment phrasing, and report-narrative fidelity rather than shipped behavior. Candidate mechanisms for the spec discussion: a severity floor below which a reviewer records a note instead of a blocking finding; a fix-round budget per task with overflow deferred as batch-report items; letting Minor-only rounds close controller-verified without a re-review dispatch; distinguishing contract surfaces (code, user-facing text, gates) from narrative surfaces (report prose) in the rules' blast radius. Needs an owner-gated spec: the mechanism must not soften process.no-tech-debt's core (real defects still get fixed) - it targets the cost of the loop, not the standard.

Ruled 2026-10-09 (design.md 5.90): the item leaves batch 29 and is built in batch 31 with HR-159, HR-160, and HR-161. The owner directed two mechanisms: a finding's severity follows its impact, not its rule's class, and the review loop is bounded - a re-review reads the fix diff against the original findings, files new findings at their impact, and only a new Critical or Important finding opens a further round.

items.title: A risk-tiered batch pipeline: the change's risk picks the review depth
body: Owner (2026-10-09, design.md 5.90): build in batch 31. Every change runs the same pipeline today: spec, owner gate, plan, code-health scan, implementer, task review on a mightier model, branch review, live run. Batch 30 shipped a 116-line workflow through 7 agent dispatches, a 353-line spec, and a 142-line plan.

Requirement: deterministic criteria (touched areas, the frozen surfaces, security-relevant paths, diff size) pick a tier at plan time; a light tier runs the gates and one review, a standard tier one review and at most one re-review, a full tier today's pipeline. The kit ships the mechanism to adopters through `houserules update`.

items.title: A self-optimizing knowledge base: rules earn their place with measured catches, and a budget caps the standing set
body: Owner (2026-10-09, design.md 5.90): build in batch 31. Knowledge only grows today: 41 entries and 26 standing at 2026-09-02, 102 and 39 at 2026-10-09; audit rows per review grew from 30 (batch 2) to 62 (batch 30). Every rule costs on every task; most catch nothing.

Requirement: a mechanism that runs at every batch close and proposes, from measured data, to retire or demote rules that caught nothing over a window, to convert a prose rule into a deterministic check, and to keep the standing set under a budget; a retrospective proposal defaults to a non-standing area entry. Owner-gated changes (standing entries, owner rulings) go to the owner as proposals; the rest apply in the batch's knowledge commit.

items.title: Adopters get the cost analysis: the shipped binary measures a workspace's process cost per rule
body: Owner (2026-10-09, design.md 5.90): build in batch 31. The analysis of 2026-10-09 ran as session scripts over this repository's workspaces. Adopters need the same measurement so that their own houserules setup self-optimizes (HR-160): reviews and fix rounds per task, findings by severity and by target (code, deliverable, prose), report size, and per rule its injections, audit rows, catches, and the findings it caused.
Constraint from the same ruling: an adopter updates after the release with as little friction as possible - no manual migration step, and no gate that reddens an existing install.

items.title: The seeded CI installs the latest binary: a release that tightens a gate reddens every install before it updates
body: Found in the batch-28 branch review. template/.github/workflows/knowledge.yml installs houserules from releases/latest, while the kit files in an adopter's tree stay at the version of its last `houserules update`. A release that adds a check to check-knowledge or check-backlog therefore runs the new check over old kit files. It has happened before. Derived from the source at the release tags, not run: the 1.1.0 binary requires AGENTS.md, and the kit files of 0.3.0 and 1.0.0 hold none, so release 1.1.0 failed check-knowledge in every earlier install until `update` backfilled the file. Batch 28 does the same through the citation lint: the finishing-a-feature skill of 0.3.0, 1.0.0, and 1.1.0 cites knowledge-base.cite-durable-refs, an id the kit never seeded, and the new citation lint fails on it until `houserules update` runs and its result is committed.

Ruled by the owner on 2026-10-02 (design.md 5.88): the seeded workflow installs the version `.houserules.json` records, and batch 28 builds it. The lint ships as built; the release note states the red first. The workflow is a seed-once file, so the change reaches new installs; an existing install edits its own workflow, and the release note says how.

Status after batch 28: partial. Built: the seeded workflow reads the top-level `version` line of `.houserules.json` with a POSIX tool and installs the installer of that release; a stamp with no such line falls back to the latest release with a notice; a version that is no release version is rejected before any download; a failed download prints a named error. The step's own script ran for real against the published releases with the home directory at a scratch directory. Two duties stay open and are due at the first release that carries the step (docs/runbook.md, the release procedure): (1) the owner-attended seeded-repository run of houserules.seeded-repo-live-proof, which is the only real Actions run of the step; (2) the release note prints the changed install step for installs that keep their seed-once workflow, and states first that check-knowledge fails in every existing install until `houserules update` runs. The item closes with the run of (1).

Closed 2026-10-02 at release 1.2.0, the first release that carries the step (design.md 5.89). (1) The seeded-repository run: the controller ran it on the owner's ruling, in the private throwaway repository jblossey/houserules-seed-proof-1-2-0, seeded by `houserules init` from the released 1.2.0 archive. Pull request 1 (stamp 1.2.0, run 36987840103): the step printed `downloading houserules 1.2.0`, and check-knowledge, check-backlog, and audit passed. Pull request 2 (the stamp edited to 1.1.0 while 1.2.0 was the latest release, run 36987907702): the step printed `downloading houserules 1.1.0`, and every step passed. The second run separates the stamped release from the latest one; the first run alone cannot. Captures: .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-01-batch-28/hr154-evidence/. (2) The 1.2.0 release note states the check-knowledge red first and prints the install step of the v1.2.0 tag; the owner approved the text. The owner deletes the throwaway repository.

items.title: Modular installs: adopters choose the feature set
body: Owner intent recorded at the Tier-2 CLI-surface ruling (2026-09-04): houserules becomes modular — an adopter can install only backlog management, or rules management without the backlog, or the full kit. This is WHY the flat command surface keeps per-module checks (check-knowledge, check-backlog) and the Rust crate separates rules, backlog, and install modules.

Shape: a feature/selection mechanism in init (and update honoring it) that installs a subset of the payload — the seeded files, generated artifacts, skills, and checks scoped to the chosen modules; the stamp records the selection. Details to the batch spec when gated, AFTER the Tier-2 port completes (the port ships everything; the crate boundaries prepare the split).
Source: owner, 2026-09-04, at the batch 15 CLI-surface ruling; the Tier-2 spec's architecture section carries the boundary design.
Owner ruling 2026-10-10 (batch-33 Q1, design.md 5.96): not in 2.0.0. It ships after 2.0.0 as a minor release under the 2.0 surface rule (D2).

Owner ruling 2026-10-16 (meta-spec O13, while it was asked): a backlog-only install, a tracker without the knowledge base, is out of scope; Beads serves that use, and it is no longer houserules' main focus. Owner, verbatim: "tracker without a knowledge base is no longer in scope. People can use beads for that. That is no longer houserules main focus."

Owner ruling 2026-10-16 (design.md 5.147, meta-spec O13): dropped. 2.0.0 delivers the in-scope parts through HR-180 (the rules without a backlog: no default tracker, 5.138), HR-182 (optional packs, 5.105), and HR-181 (an optional workflow, 5.111); the remaining part, a backlog-only install, is out of scope. This replaces Q1's 'ships after 2.0.0 as a minor' for this item.

items.title: Main needs the code owner's approval for everyone but the owner; Dependabot auto-merge runs on the owner's token
body: Owner ruling 2026-09-11: only the owner merges to main without an approval; every other contributor's PR needs the owner's approving review. Applied as a second ruleset `approval` on the default branch (one approving review, code-owner review required, stale reviews dismissed on push, threads resolved) whose only bypass actor is the repository admin role. The first ruleset `main` (the eight required checks incl. CodeQL, linear history, no force-push, PR required) keeps no bypass and binds the owner too. GitHub cannot exempt one rule inside a ruleset, hence the split.

Consequence and the ruled fix: GitHub refuses the Actions app as a bypass actor on a user-owned repository, so a merge enabled with GITHUB_TOKEN now waits for an approval and the HR-092 auto-merge stalls. The owner chose the token route: .github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml enables auto-merge with a fine-grained personal access token of the owner (Contents and Pull requests read/write on this repository only), stored as the Dependabot secret DEPENDABOT_AUTOMERGE_TOKEN (a Dependabot-triggered workflow reads that store, not Actions secrets). A merge performed as the owner also starts the push workflows on main, which lifts HR-092's GITHUB_TOKEN limit for these merges.

PENDING proof: the next minor or patch Dependabot PR merging on its own with the workflow green. Flip to done with that PR's number. HR-068 (a token for the release flow) stays a separate ruling: release-please edits a workflow file, which needs the `workflows` permission this token does not carry.

Proof run, read 2026-10-01: negative. PR #31 (clap 4.6.6 to 4.6.7, a patch) got auto-merge enabled by the owner's token eleven seconds after it opened on 2026-09-18, then waited: it merged on 2026-09-21, seconds after the owner's own approving review. The token enables auto-merge; it does not satisfy the approval ruleset, because an enabled auto-merge waits for every requirement and the admin bypass does not apply to it. PRs #33 and #34 (github/codeql-action analyze and init, 4.38.0 to 4.38.1, opened 2026-09-25) stand blocked on two counts: the approving review is still required, and both CodeQL `analyze` jobs fail on each PR - Dependabot bumps the two actions in separate PRs, and they must share one version. PR #33 (analyze at 4.38.1) prints `Loaded a configuration file for version '4.38.0', but running version '4.38.1'`; PR #34 (init at 4.38.1) prints the same line with the two versions exchanged. PR #32 (dependabot/fetch-metadata 2.5.0 to 3.1.0, a major) is approved, carries no auto-merge by design, and is behind main.

Repair ruled 2026-10-01 (design.md 5.87): the workflow approves a minor or patch Dependabot PR with the owner's token before it enables auto-merge, and a Dependabot group moves the `github/codeql-action` pair in one PR. The item closes on the first minor or patch Dependabot PR that merges with no owner action.

Proof run 2, read 2026-10-02: the repair works as built, and the merge still waits. Dependabot closed PRs #33, #34, #44, and #45. It opened PR #48 (the `codeql-action` group, both steps in one PR) at 08:27:16 UTC, after batch 28 reached main. items.title: Lifecycle: an adversarial review gate in the design phase
body: GitHub issue #38 (owner, 2026-09-30). The batch lifecycle reviews code three times (implementer self-review, task reviewer, branch reviewer) and reviews design zero times: the Design row of the orchestrating skill asks only for a spec and the owner's approval, so the owner is the first and only adversarial check on a design decision. The issue reports from the adopter project orrery: in one batch and one spec draft, four design decisions were overturned, each refuted by a cheap check. Named causes: the controller argued before it tested, did not state the rejected option's best case, and inherited concepts unexamined.

Request, three parts. (1) A design-phase gate in the lifecycle table and the orchestrating skill: before the owner sees a spec, a fresh-context reviewer on the strongest model attacks its decisions and reruns its probes, and its findings are fixed. (2) A `spec-reviewer` agent template beside `task-reviewer` and `branch-reviewer`, and a `spec-review` deliverable kind in .claude/schemas/deliverables.json, so `houserules validate` and `houserules stats` cover it. (3) Seed rules for the design phase: a decision that rejects a library or departs from the source research or an approved spec carries a captured probe, the rejected option's best case, and a reversal condition; each supporting claim is labelled run, read, or assumed, and an assumed claim is never the sole reason for a rejection; a spec lists every concept it takes from its sources, with the source's own status and a check against the goal; every decision the owner or a reviewer overturns is a `Reversal:` ledger line, and the batch retrospective counts reversals beside rule violations.

Triage 2026-10-01: part 2 adds a deliverable kind to both parity-pinned copies of the deliverables schema, a frozen surface (houserules.1-0-surface-is-frozen): it needs an owner ruling on whether the addition is a breaking change. The gate adds a review round to the lifecycle, so its design must be weighed against HR-140 (the balancing mechanism against over-bureaucratizing). A new kit-owned template changes KIT_OWNED (houserules.readme-mirrors-kit-owned).

items.title: The kit installs into a subdirectory of a repository
body: GitHub issue #41 (external reporter, 2026-10-01). The reporter could not use houserules in one subdirectory of a large legacy monorepo: an install at the repository root required moving files that belong to other domains. Request: remove the repository-root requirement. The issue names no version, no command, and no output.

Triage 2026-10-01, reproduced with the 1.1.0 tree: in a subdirectory of a git repository, `houserules init` and `houserules init --dir .` both refuse with `<dir> is not a git repository (run git init first)`. The message is wrong for this case: the directory is inside a repository, and `git init` there would create a nested one.

Scope for the spec: every read command resolves the enclosing git top level as its root; `init` requires the target to be one; the seeded hooks, the CI workflow, and the `.claude/` directory assume the repository root. A subdirectory install changes that contract across the CLI, so it needs its own spec and an owner ruling under houserules.1-0-surface-is-frozen. The error text can be corrected on its own.
Ruled 2026-10-01 (design.md 5.87): batch 28 corrects the refusal text; the subdirectory install stays open here for its own spec.

Status after batch 28: partial. The refusal text shipped: a target inside a repository gets `<target> is inside the git repository at <top level>, not its top level; houserules installs at the repository root`, derived from the nearest ancestor that holds `.git`. The subdirectory install itself stays open for its own spec.
Owner ruling 2026-10-10 (batch-33 decision D7, design.md 5.96): the subdirectory install gets its own batch after 2.0.0 (batch 34), as a minor release under the 2.0 surface rule.
On 2026-10-15 the owner ruled that every open GitHub issue ships in 2.0.0 (design.md 5.98): this item moves to batch 33; this supersedes D7 (batch 34).

Owner ruling 2026-10-16 (design.md 5.135, meta-spec O3), delivered with this item: every command defaults to the nearest directory at or above the current directory that holds .houserules.json, no higher than the git top level, else the git top level; init --dir <subdir> installs there; .claude/ and .githooks/ live in the install root and the docs say to launch Claude Code there; houserules never sets core.hooksPath, and the docs give both activations (core.hooksPath, or a call from an existing hook manager); in a subdirectory install check-commit checks only the commits that touch the install root (staged files for the hook, each commit's changed paths for --from) and prints a count of the skipped commits.

Owner ruling 2026-10-19 (design.md 5.168), delivered with this item: one repository may hold several installs; each subdirectory install gets its own seeded CI workflow .github/workflows/knowledge-<folder>.yml at the git top level, tracked and rewritten by update through a baseline; an install at the git top level keeps knowledge.yml.

items.title: Implementer template: the closing check-report-claims run must not redirect into its own capture
body: Found by the batch-28 eval rerun (docs-edit) and by the batch-28 task-4 implementer. The closing act tells the implementer to run `houserules check-report-claims <REPORT_FILE>` and paste its clean run as the final `tests` entry. The `tests` contract asks for a redirect to a capture file. A re-run of that entry with the same redirect truncates the capture before the checker reads it, and the checker then fails the entry on a byte mismatch. The implementers worked around it: one left the closing entry without a redirect, one re-checked into a second file.

Scope for the fix: one sentence in the closing act of template/.claude/agents/implementer.md that states the form of the final entry (no redirect, or a capture file no earlier entry names). The change needs the eval rerun (process.evals-rerun).

Added by the batch-28 branch review: the same closing sequence has a second gap. The closing act says 'Not clean: fix the report and re-run'. That fix can edit a cited sentence after the citation step ran, and no step sends the implementer back. Add one sentence: after a fix to the report, repeat the citation step, then the closing run. Both edits share one eval rerun.

items.title: Citation remedy side effects: an id active and archived at once; update without a stamp resets the id prefix
body: Found in the batch-28 branch review and its fix wave (HR-146). (1) An adopter who archived a seeded entry that a kit-owned file cites, and then follows the restore remedy of check-knowledge, gets the entry back as active while knowledge/archive/ keeps the retired copy. No gate reports the id held twice. (2) `houserules update` on an install with no `.houserules.json` stamps `idPrefix` from `--id-prefix` or `WI`; the restore remedy says 'run houserules update', so a project with its own prefix and no stamp gets `WI` unless it passes the flag. (3) For a whole deleted seeded topic file, the `overrides` way out clears the citation findings but leaves dangling `see` links, and check-knowledge stays red on those.

(4) On an install with no stamp, the `overrides` way out does not keep the entry deleted past the next `update`: no baseline records the deletion, so `update` completes the stamp and writes the entry back as active. Points 1 to 3 are stated in the doc of the lint and pinned by a test in batch 28; point 4 was measured in the scoped re-review of the branch fix wave and has neither. None is changed there. Scope for a spec: decide whether check-knowledge reports an id that is both active and archived; whether the remedy names the `--id-prefix` flag for an unstamped install; whether the deleted-topic case gets its own remedy text.

items.title: Template and rule riders from the batch-28 branch review
body: Deferred from batch 28 into batch 29, which redesigns the review mechanism and these same templates (HR-144, HR-140, HR-129). Template defects, each with the reviewer's fix: (1) orchestrating skill: a task that adds or tightens a check in check-knowledge, check-backlog, or audit carries a paper walk in its brief (a fresh install, an install on each released kit under the new binary, an install with kept or overridden kit-owned files), and the report states each accepted red. (2) orchestrating skill, the rule that a brief's claims are measured: a brief that dictates a message reads it once for each state that prints it; a brief that dictates an enumeration derives it from the subject, never from a file name; a brief that dictates a mechanism a reviewer proposed has run it against the reviewer's own counter-example first (eight of the 31 task-review findings of batch 28 were plan-mandated). (3) branch-reviewer template: compare BASE with the remote default branch through a read-only call; list the commits in BASE..HEAD that no task report lists and review each. (4) finishing-a-feature skill, the aggregation step: fetch first; if main moved, rebuild the branch on it before the soft reset.

Clauses the review proposes for standing entries; only the owner rules these: process.claims-match-artifacts (a fix round that re-runs or re-pins an earlier round's evidence says so; a line citation into a generated evidence file is re-derived after each regeneration); process.closure-claims-carry-enumeration (a corpus of deliverables is selected by content, never by file name; an exception list is a closure with its own script); process.gates-cover-generated-commits (a check added to a shipped gate is walked through the installed populations, and the new predicate runs over the template at each release tag); process.rulings-to-file (a brief amendment that adds or drops a test, a file, or a gate against the plan is a ruling for the spec's outcomes section); writing-style.code-comments (a comment on measured or third-party behavior names an openable source; the controller files the knowledge entry before the dispatch); writing-style.doc-comments (a new caller re-opens the callee's doc comment); process.tdd (a RED against a stub of an implementation already drafted is a `mutation` entry).

Added from the batch-30 branch review (2026-10-02), deferred because batch 30 changes nothing under template/. Clauses for the kit-shipped entry knowledge-base.state-only-the-source: a premise about a third-party platform is quoted from the page's own sentence before a brief or an entry restates it; the sweep for a corrected fact is a grep for its key nouns over the tracked tree and the batch documents, in the commit that corrects it. Clauses for standing entries, which only the owner rules: process.claims-match-artifacts (a claim about a documentation page quotes every passage of the page that bears on it, and says which one the measurement supports when two disagree; a duration is recomputed from its two timestamps before the sentence ships, a rounded word included); writing-style.code-comments (a doc comment written in a fix round is swept for the round's own vocabulary before the commit, and the fix-round dispatch names the sweep). Template defects: (1) orchestrating skill, the fix-round closing rule: say which default wins for a prose-only round that closes a finding that is critical by rule class. (2) orchestrating skill and branch-reviewer template: no text covers a branch rebuilt on a moved main (the sha map, the old history, what the reviewer checks) or a loaded template that is older than the file at HEAD. (3) task-reviewer and branch-reviewer templates: 'real severity' conflicts with 'standing rule critical' for a one-word prose mismatch; a finding whose severity comes from the rule class says so first and states the size of the repair. (4) deliverables schema and implementer template: a task report of batch 30 is 267 KB, 154 KB of it pasted output in `tests`; allowing an output file with a line count for a long output needs an owner ruling, because the schema is frozen.
Owner ruling 2026-10-20 (design.md 179): the clause for process.rulings-to-file is refused.

Owner ruling 2026-10-20 (design.md 183, batch-34 spec Q5): eight standing-entry clauses approved; the writing-style.code-comments clause 'the controller files the knowledge entry before the dispatch' refused.

Batch 34 record: its two defects that assume severity by rule class close as superseded by process.severity-by-impact (batch-34 spec C13, 9.1); its long-output question goes to HR-171 in batch 36. The other defects and the clauses of design.md 183 shipped in batch 34.

items.title: Seeded topic files ship in the form emit writes, so a first update rewrites nothing
body: Found in batch 31 task 2 (live run of the adopter update path). `update` re-emits every seeded knowledge topic file through `emit`; template/knowledge/quality.json and template/knowledge/security-hygiene.json are stored compact, so the first `update` of a fresh install reformats them (76 and 96 lines of whitespace). main's 1.2.0 binary updating a fresh 1.2.0 install produces the same diff, so the noise predates batch 31.

Fix: store every seeded topic file in emit's form, and add a test that `update` right after `init` leaves the knowledge files byte-identical. This lowers the friction of every adopter update (HR-161's constraint).

items.title: Batch-31 retrospective proposals that change code or the two eval-covered templates
body: From the batch-31 branch review retrospective (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-09-batch-31/branch-review.json, violated_rules). Deferred out of batch 31 because each changes executable code or the implementer or task-reviewer template, which re-opens the eval run (process.evals-rerun) for a batch already past it.

1. Generate README's sample `stats` output as a frozen slice and assert the README block equals it (quality.user-facing-text-is-contract). 2. Enable rustdoc missing_docs for the crate's public items (writing-style.doc-comments). 3. check-report-claims reads backlog items and specs: a cited workspace path exists, and a cited stats run names the file that holds its window (process.claims-match-artifacts). 4. Implementer template, TDD step: a pin of existing behavior runs at BASE first and records the passing exit beside its disclosed mutation (process.tdd). 5. Task-reviewer template: a closure probe derives from the claim's subject, and an instruction keyed to a tier, count, or version is read once per value of that field (process.closure-claims-carry-enumeration, writing-style.instructions-cover-the-state-space). 6. The finishing-a-feature skill's Finish step runs `houserules check-commit --from <merge base>` with the tree binary when the batch changes the binary, since the commit-msg hook skips the check when no houserules is on PATH (batch-31 branch review, template defect 4, second half).

7. From the batch-32 branch review retrospective (process.tdd): the implementer template's fix-round contract gains one sentence. A test the fix round adds that passes before the fix gets a `mutation` tdd row in that round, with the mutation diff captured. The re-reviewer checks that every such test has one.
Batch 34 record: point 2's missing_docs scope is the crate's public items: crates/houserules/src/main.rs sets #![warn(missing_docs)]. That also delivers HR-204 item 9 (batch-34 spec 9.1).

items.title: Four Minor findings left at the batch-31 fix-wave cap: the until clause, two texts, one report citation

1. The summary-is-the-rule check's until clause stops at any period, so 'until 1.3.0 ships' escapes it; use (?:[^.;:]|\.\d){0,40} in both copies and add the phrase to the test's PHRASES. 2. The entry body and the test module doc say each word carries a bracketed letter; each branch of the pattern does. 3. items.title: Template defects: the implementer's self-audit file, the exit-code form, and several workspaces per batch
body: Source: an adopter's lead-time audit of its batch 3 under houserules 1.2.0 (2026-10-10; design.md 5.94). Issues 5 and 10.

1. implementer.md names no file for the implementer's own audit run. The adopter's implementer wrote it to task-7-audit.json, the reviewer's AUDIT_JSON, and later to the re-review's path; `houserules stats` reads every task-*-audit*.json, so the batch record changed. The template states that the self-audit lives only in the report's self_audit and that the implementer writes no task-* file other than REPORT_FILE, as task-reviewer.md already states for the reviewer.

2. implementer.md forbids `;` and `|` in a captured command. An adopter rule prescribed `<command>; echo "EXIT=$?"`. The template states that the entry's `exit` field carries the exit status and that a command never appends an echo of it.

3. branch-reviewer.md assumes one workspace per batch. A batch that adds a second spec part-way has two. The dispatch names every workspace of the batch; the branch reviewer runs the workspace audit once per workspace and reads all of them, as `houserules stats` already does.

items.title: Standing rules that govern only the controller's acts stay out of task audits
body: Source: an adopter's lead-time audit of its batch 3 under houserules 1.2.0 (2026-10-10; design.md 5.94). Issue 6.

Measured over this repository's 266 task reviews (7,806 judged rows): six kit standing rules whose subject is an act only the controller performs (process.brainstorm-first, process.backlog-drives-work, process.code-health-scan, process.model-policy, process.live-run-before-ci, process.owner-rulings-need-owner-supersession) and quality.well-maintained-libraries were judged 1,745 times in task reviews with 0 fails. Every standing rule sits in a glob-less area (global or process), so a file-pattern engagement test would remove no row.

Change: an entry tagged `controller` governs the controller's acts. A task audit (`houserules audit` with `--report`) leaves an entry tagged `controller` out of its package unless `--ids` names it, standing or not; the branch audit (`--workspace`) and a plain audit keep it. The kit tags its controller rules. In a batch without a branch review, the controller judges the controller rows of the branch-range audit before Finish. A tag is a free string of the knowledge schema: no schema change, no new flag.

items.title: A loading path for non-standing process rules
body: Source: an adopter's lead-time audit of its batch 3 under houserules 1.2.0 (2026-10-10; design.md 5.94). Issue 7.

The seed gives the `process` area no file patterns, and knowledge-base.rules-need-a-loading-path names standing as the only other loading path, so an adopter's process rule ends up standing: judged in every audit and loaded in every session. 1.3.0 added citation loading, but only kit-owned skills and templates cite ids, and `update` overwrites them.

Change: name the loading paths a non-standing process rule already has. The controller reads every process entry's summary at each session start (the orchestrating skill's ritual, `houserules index --area process`); an agent receives the ids the controller puts on its `Knowledge:` line. The entry body, the orchestrating skill, and the migrating-knowledge skill state these paths and say that a process rule is standing only when every session must carry it; a rule only the controller can break also gets the `controller` tag.

items.title: Review findings name the caller their fix serves and the check that closes a Minor
body: Source: an adopter's lead-time audit of its batch 3 under houserules 1.2.0 (2026-10-10; design.md 5.94). Issue 2, the part 1.3.0 left open.

A Minor asked for a hashable type that no caller hashes; its fix broke asdict and deepcopy and needed a second fix round. 1.3.0 closes a Minor-only round on a controller note, but the note's check is the controller's choice and no later step reads the closures.

Change: a finding whose fix adds a capability names the caller that needs it; without one, the implementer may contest it and the controller drops it or files it. Each Minor finding states the check that proves its fix (a command and its expected result); the controller runs that check for its verification note. The branch reviewer re-runs a sample of the controller notes. A seeded-violations expectation pins that a standing-rule slip of Minor impact is filed Minor.

items.title: Narrow process.rulings-to-file: a decision inside the spec's intent goes to the brief, not a spec amendment
body: Source: an adopter's lead-time audit of its batch 3 under houserules 1.2.0 (2026-10-10; design.md 5.94). Root cause 9.

process.rulings-to-file counts every dispatch deviation from the spec as a ruling to amend in the same turn. The adopter's controller made nine plan-sync docs commits for decisions such as a status code or a tuple type.

Proposal: only a decision that changes what the spec states amends the spec; a decision inside the spec's intent is recorded in the task brief or the task report, and the branch review reads it there. The entry is standing and owner-seeded: it needs the owner's ruling before any build (process.owner-rulings-need-owner-supersession).
Owner ruling 2026-10-16 (design.md 5.147, meta-spec O13): joins batch 34 (2.0.0, batch 2 of 5); its standing-entry ruling is taken at the batch-34 spec review, with HR-153's standing clauses (D10).

Owner ruling 2026-10-20 (design.md 179, batch-34 spec Q1): narrow as proposed; only a decision that changes what the spec states amends the spec; a decision inside the spec's intent goes to the brief or report.

items.title: A Dependabot PR that falls behind main waits: the ruleset requires an up-to-date branch, and no rebase is promised
body: Found at the batch-28 rollout on PR #48 (HR-098, proof run 2). The `main` ruleset requires an up-to-date branch. A push to main while a Dependabot PR is open leaves the PR behind, and its enabled auto-merge then waits. GitHub's documentation promises an automatic Dependabot rebase only for conflicts ('Managing pull requests for dependency updates', read 2026-10-02: 'By default, Dependabot automatically rebases pull requests to resolve any conflicts'). What Dependabot did on its own after one of its PRs merged is in the last paragraph.

Evidence from this repository's PR timelines, read 2026-10-02. PR #32 was behind main from 2026-09-21. The weekly runs of 2026-09-25 and 2026-10-02 (about 03:55 UTC, Fridays) opened new PRs and did not rebase it. The run that batch 28's change of .github/dependabot.yml started did rebase behind PRs: it force-pushed PR #32 and PR #43 at 08:26 UTC on 2026-10-02. PR #43 changes only .github/workflows/ci.yml, which batch 28 did not touch, so that rebase resolved no conflict.

Owner rulings 2026-10-02 (design.md 5.89). First ruling: observe the weekly run of 2026-10-09. The controller then found the PR #32 evidence above, which it had not read before it asked, and proposed the reversal. Second ruling, which supersedes the first: design the fix now, as batch 30, before batch 29. PR #48 stays untouched and is the proof.

More evidence, read 2026-10-02 after PR #48 merged (10:39:38 UTC, see HR-098). Dependabot ran at 10:41 and force-pushed PRs #32 and #43 at 10:41:40 and 10:41:46; both then read `behind_by=0`. The three PRs change three different workflow files, so that rebase resolved no conflict. That is one observation, not a rule. The others: PR #32 (github-actions) stayed behind after PR #31 (cargo) merged on 2026-09-21; the release commit, a push by the owner, left PR #48 behind for almost two hours; the batch-28 push, which changed .github/dependabot.yml, was followed by rebases of PRs #32 and #43 two minutes later. The stall that this item fixes is the observed one: a push to main after which Dependabot does not rebase. PR #48 can no longer be the proof; the proof is the first run of the workflow that finds a behind PR with auto-merge on. Owner ruling 2026-10-02 at the branch review: the workflow skips a PR whose checks have failed at its current head (spec section 8).

items.title: The seeded CI gate runs on GitLab as well as GitHub
body: Owner direction, 2026-10-10, at the batch-33 (2.0.0) preparation: the CI workflow must also suit projects that use GitLab instead of GitHub.

Today init and update write .github/workflows/knowledge.yml only when remote.origin.url contains github.com (install.rs GITHUB_HOSTED_SEED_ONCE, origin_is_github_hosted). Every other host gets a skip note, and the migrating-knowledge skill ('Generate your own CI gate') tells the adopter to write the gate by hand. The finishing-a-feature skill names only gh commands.

Change: a seeded GitLab CI gate that runs the same three steps (check-knowledge, check-backlog, audit on a merge request) and installs the stamped version; a host choice that also covers self-managed GitLab; GitLab steps in finishing-a-feature; a live proof in a real GitLab pipeline. Design: batch-33 spec, decision D11.

Dropped by the owner on 2026-10-10 (batch-33 decision D11, design.md 5.96): the current behavior is enough. On a host other than GitHub, init prints a note, and the migrating-knowledge skill says what to set up in the CI pipeline and how.

items.title: Seed knowledge-base.cite-durable-refs (issue 50)
body: GitHub issue 50 asks the kit to seed knowledge-base.cite-durable-refs. Design.md 5.88 ruled the entry not seeded; the owner superseded that on 2026-10-10 (batch-33 decision D6, design.md 5.96).
